includes: openclaw update and every subcommand (status, repair, cleanup, wizard), the --update shorthand, the update.* Gateway methods, the /update chat command, the Control UI Updates settings section, the sidebar update card and the update overlays: this area's operations
docs/web/control-ui/settings.md: only its Updates section describes this area; every other section of that page belongs to other areas and is not read for entry points or conditions

docs/gateway/telemetry.md: only its 'Daily update check', 'Automated environments' and 'Disable every automatic update request' sections describe this area; docs/tools/slash-commands.md: only the /update and /restart commands and the commands.restart and commands.ownerAllowFrom settings describe this area; the rest of both pages is not read for entry points or conditions
docs/install/docker.md: only its 'Upgrading container images' section describes this area; the rest of the page belongs to install

release channels (stable, extended-stable, beta, dev), --channel and --tag targeting, dry runs and the configured update channel (docs/install/development-channels.md): this area; switching channel is an operation, the configured channel is a condition
automatic updates: the auto-updater, update.checkOnStart, update.auto.*, update campaigns, the startup update check and the headless node host's own updates (src/node-host/auto-update*.ts): this area

Doctor's update repairs: Doctor as the updater runs it (post-upgrade Doctor, candidate migration rehearsal, schema guard, update refusal), config migrations (docs/gateway/doctor/config-migrations.md), legacy file-backed state migrations (docs/cli/doctor/state-migrations.md) and schema version bumps and refusals (docs/reference/database-schemas/versioning.md): this area; openclaw doctor and openclaw doctor --fix are entry points here only for these repairs

rollback and recovery: update rollback, compatibility-checked package rollback, the retained updater runtime, update repair, update cleanup, downgrade recovery (docs/reference/database-schemas/integrity-and-recovery.md 'Why you cannot go back after updating', 'The Gateway refuses to start with a newer schema version error', 'Downgrade recovery', and 'Doctor reports orphan task delivery rows', which docs/cli/update.md cites for update admission) and openclaw triage for failed update recovery (docs/cli/triage.md): this area

restart after update: the restart handoff, the restart sentinel and post-update notice, openclaw gateway restart, gateway.restart.request, gateway.restart.preflight and /restart (docs/cli/gateway/restart-and-supervision.md), the graceful drain before a restart and recovery after a failed update (docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md 'Graceful restarts drain first', 'Recovery after a failed update', 'Verify recovery after an update'): this area
openclaw status: only its update and restart lines (src/commands/status.update.ts, src/commands/status-update-restart.ts) are entry points here

updating by another method: re-running the installer over an existing installation, manual npm, pnpm, bun or Homebrew installs over it and switching between npm and git installs (docs/install/updating/update-methods.md): this area's operation; the installer scripts themselves are owned by install

plugin sync during openclaw update (docs/cli/update/how-updates-run.md 'Plugin sync details') and plugin-provided state migrations Doctor runs (docs/cli/doctor/state-migrations.md 'Pending plugin migrations'): entry points here; plugin code reached this way is listed as kind from plugins
the state an update migrates (sessions, cron, channels, pairing, exec approvals, auth, media, transcripts) is a condition of this area, not an operation of the area that owns that state

the step 2 caller search greps exactly the symbols and literals under search, as whole words, over src, ui/src, extensions and packages; every non-test file outside paths that it finds is one entry point of kind from <area>, including Doctor files of the session store import and config files, whose own operations stay with their areas; matches in test harnesses, QA lab extensions and repository scripts are listed once per file under excluded entry points as test-only

this area's startup hooks and scheduled jobs are one entry point each, kind startup hook or scheduled job: the startup update check, the periodic update check, the automatic update campaign, the update run watcher, restart sentinel processing at startup, the restart-update-run finalization after the replacement Gateway starts, startup state migration with its checkpoint, legacy update admission expiry, startup failure triage, the installation replacement check on the maintenance tick, pending package lifecycle completion before a CLI command, automatic triage after a failed managed update, and the headless node host's automatic update

updating by another method is one entry point each, kind another method: re-running the installer, npm install -g, pnpm add -g, bun add -g, brew upgrade openclaw-cli, replacing a container image over the same mounted state, and scripts/update-gateway.sh

choices inside an interactive terminal prompt (the failure menu after a failed update, the triage launch consent, the downgrade confirmation) are not entry points; they are conditions of the command that shows them
the Settings → Updates route itself is navigation and is listed with the shell controls, not as its own entry point

commands and methods of other areas that the documents name as follow-up or diagnostic steps are listed once each under excluded entry points as consumed from <area>, one line per command or method: openclaw gateway start, openclaw gateway stop, openclaw gateway status, openclaw gateway install, openclaw gateway call, openclaw health, openclaw logs, openclaw nodes status, openclaw node restart, openclaw config get, openclaw config set, openclaw config validate, openclaw database preflight, openclaw database ownership claim, openclaw completion, openclaw plugins update, gateway.suspend.prepare, gateway.suspend.status, gateway.suspend.resume, gateway.suspend.handoff, config.get, config.patch, channels.start, chat.send; openclaw daemon restart is listed as excluded, deprecated
excludes: automatic resume of interrupted turns and subagents after a restart (docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md 'Automatic resume', 'Subagents', 'Agent-requested restarts'; src/agents/main-session-recovery/**; src/gateway/server-methods/chat-restart-recovery.ts), the legacy session store import (openclaw doctor --session-sqlite, docs/gateway/doctor/state-and-sessions.md) and session store schema: owned by sessions
openclaw plugins install, update and uninstall, src/plugins/update*.ts, src/cli/plugins-update-*.ts and the plugin SDK migration guides (docs/plugins/sdk-migration*): owned by plugins

config read, write, save, backups, reload (src/gateway/server-reload-*.ts), redaction and schema (config get, set, patch, schema and the config.* Gateway methods): owned by config; config migrations applied by Doctor or by an update stay in this area

channel setup, routing and delivery: owned by channels; channel config and ownership migrations during an update (docs/gateway/doctor/config-migrations.md 'Channel account routing during an update', 'Channel ownership during an update') stay in this area as conditions
openclaw migrate and migrations.memory.* (importing from other assistants; docs/cli/migrate.md, docs/install/migrating*.md, src/commands/migrate/**): owned by migrate
openclaw backup (docs/cli/backup.md, docs/install/backups.md): owned by backup; creating a verified backup before an update is listed as an entry point of kind from backup
fresh installation (install.sh, install-cli.sh, install.ps1, docs/install/installer.md, onboarding): owned by install

Doctor checks that are neither update repairs nor migrations (gateway service recovery in docs/cli/doctor/recovery.md, the health contract, lint, SQLite maintenance, integrity checks other than the newer-schema refusal and downgrade recovery): owned by doctor
docs/reference/team-immutable-update-design.md: a design proposal, not a description of current behaviour; immutable release installations are read from docs/cli/update.md
openclaw claws update and src/claws/**: owned by claws; openclaw hooks update and src/hooks/update.ts: owned by hooks
device scope upgrades (src/gateway/device-scope-upgrade.ts, ui/src/app/device-scope-upgrade*.ts): owned by devices

Gateway protocol versioning between clients (docs/gateway/protocol/versioning.md): owned by the Gateway protocol; a protocol mismatch after a rollback (docs/gateway/troubleshooting/updates-and-rollbacks.md) stays a condition here
macOS and mobile app self-updates (docs/platforms/macos.md update card): owned by the apps

Windows Scheduled Task paths (src/daemon/schtasks-update-recovery.ts, src/infra/windows-task-restart.ts, the update's Windows preflight): owned by platform; a break that needs Windows is outside this template's reach
release validation and CI (docs/ci/release-validation*, docs/reference/full-release-validation*): the maintainers' release process, not a user operation
